body: It’s been a harrowing start to the season for Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

Manchester United’s women are bottom of the WSL after two games, Michael Carrick is already under pressure after an unconvincing early spell in the Premier League was compounded by a League Cup defeat to Brighton in midweek, while Sir Jim’s other football projects, Nice and Lausanne, are both also rock bottom of their respective leagues in France and Switzerland.
“Built for more,” is a slogan Ineos have used in the past. The aforementioned teams sure need a bit more than they’ve produced so far this season.
The former Hearts manager, who arrived at United in August, endured a 5-0 loss against Chelsea last Sunday after beginning with a 2-1 defeat at London City Lionesses.

articles.title: Chess: Nigel Short to play at south pole in event criticised over climate impact
articles.summary: The former world title challenger, 61, will take on representatives from five other continents in a tournament rated by the global chess body Fide. Nigel Short, the 1993 world title challenger, will head to the Antarctic for his next tournament as the 61-year-old, formerly of Bolton but resident…
body: There is history for the very strongest grandmasters successfully defying the ravages of time: Emanuel Lasker in his mid-60s at Moscow 1935 and 1936, Viktor Korchnoi in his seventies, and, most impressive of all, Vasily Smyslov reaching the 1984 Candidates final against Garry Kasparov at 63.

Short is now Fide’s director for chess development. His opponents will represent all the other five inhabited continents, including three women and several Fide officials. Detractors of the event, who criticise its carbon footprint, suggest that it is too easy for him and that he could perform equally well with a simultaneous display.

However, the associated physical requirements will be challenging. The participants will have to fly from Cape Town, South Africa directly into Antarctica’s interior, a journey of more than 2,500 miles across the Southern Ocean. They will then continue to the south pole in a small aircraft designed for remote polar operations, a further seven hour journey. The event is financed by private anonymous sponsors with an interest in promoting the game.

articles.title: Derby day deluge - five things to watch in the EFL
articles.summary: Local rivalries, competitive cities, or simply a team named Derby coming to town - here are five things to look out across the weekend in the EFL.
body: A match between a relegated club and a team who missed out on a play-off spot on the final day of the season sounds like a treat - but for fans of Burnley and Derby County, it is a recipe for a potential nightmare.
The Clarets are bottom and still looking for their first win; Derby have amassed just four points in seven games and are on a three-match losing streak.
It is too early to say both are relegation candidates but the signs are worrying and Saturday's meeting at Turf Moor (15:00 BST) feels like it will carry more weight than it should.
What is worse for the Rams is Sweden international goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom has been ruled out of the match with a knee problem.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney’s cartoonish provocation has sparked a culture war but let’s just admit sport can be sexy | Emma John
articles.summary: Yes sport is about effort, sweat and inclusivity – but it also turns elite athletes into magnificent specimens of humanity where the aesthetic is part of the appeal. Have you seen the 40-second video that will change the way you think about women’s sport, women’s bodies, just, you know, women?
body: It starts with some carefully curated passive-aggression – “Dear Sydney”, “Hey Sydney”, “Respectfully Sydney” – and follows up with clips of what, in its own words, “a woman in sport actually looks like”. It shows its subject pounding the treadmill or powering down the back straight, flooring a rival with a tackle or a roundhouse kick, lifting weights or throwing herself through the air. It is, inevitably, soundtracked by Dua Lipa. Training Season is getting a serious bump this week.

The almighty backlash to the Novig advert that everyone would rather not have talked about at all has generated more montages than we’ve seen since Rocky IV. My own feed is swamped with inspo-insta reels from grassroots and elite athletes alike. Some might argue it’s the best thing to happen to women’s sport this week – unless, you know, they’re the European Solheim Cup team. Either way, a positively cartoonish piece of provocation lit the five-second fuse to the powder-keg stamped CULTURE WAR, and the resultant explosion has enveloped us all in its cloud of colourful outrage and content confetti.

articles.title: Todd Boehly exits Chelsea diminished after having his fingers burned
articles.summary: The billionaire’s departure will change little day-to-day but could be significant for club’s stadium plans. Not since a doomed foray into the thorny world of the transfer market has Todd Boehly had any real influence over the day-to-day at Chelsea.
body: Clearlake Capital, the US private equity firm founded by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, was already the majority owner and guiding force. The trio of Boehly, Walter and the Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss had an equal share of a 38.5% stake but have drifted into irrelevance since the BlueCo consortium bought Chelsea from Roman Abramovich for £2.5bn in 2022.
Clearlake, with Eghbali taking a prominent role, called the shots long before Wednesday night’s confirmation that it has full control after buying out Boehly and Walter.

This split has been in the works for a while. It is two years since cracks within the ownership group spilled into public. There was talk of Boehly losing faith in his working relationship with Clearlake. Boehly wanted a resolution. People close to Boehly said he had investors ready to provide capital for a full takeover, although that drew eye-rolling from Clearlake.

Its response was to consider buying Boehly out. Another suggestion from Clearlake was for Boehly to step down as chair and accept changes to governance that would leave the billionaire in little more than a ceremonial role.

articles.title: Elding ready for Irish chance after passport delay
articles.summary: Hibernian striker Owen Elding receives his first official call-up to the Republic of Ireland senior squad for the start of their Nations League campaign.
body: The 20-year-old was included in Heimir Hallgrimsson's squad for friendlies against Qatar and Canada in May and June, but only as a training player.
He was ineligible to feature in those games as he was still waiting for his Irish citizenship to come through, though Hallgrimsson invited him into camp to get a better look at the youngster.
Elding was born in England but has lived in the Republic of Ireland from the age of six, when his family made the move after his father Anthony signed for Sligo Rovers.

He therefore qualifies for the Republic of Ireland on residency grounds and he began the process of applying for Irish citizenship last year, but there was a bizarre reason for the delay that left him unable to pull on the green shirt in the last international window: fuel protests in the Republic of Ireland in April led to the cancellation of a mandatory ceremony to receive his Irish passport.

articles.title: From depression after Chelsea injury to playing non-league at 37
articles.summary: Sam Hutchinson is getting ready to play for Farnham Town in the second qualifying round of the FA Cup - 19 years after making his Chelsea debut under Jose Mourinho.
body: Sam Hutchinson played under both Jose Mourinho and Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea, set up a goal for Frank Lampard, and was in Munich on the historic night they won the Champions League for the first time in 2012.
His time at Chelsea, however, was "filled with regret and what might have been" after a chronic knee injury so nearly ended his career before it had properly started.

A product of Chelsea's youth system, Hutchinson was a promising defender on the fringes of the first team before being diagnosed with a chondral defect (a hole in his right knee) after suffering a serious injury during a reserve game at Aston Villa.

Having joined Chelsea as a seven-year-old, made his first-team debut at 17 under Mourinho and captained England at Under-19s level, Hutchinson took the gut-wrenching decision to retire at the age of 21 in 2010 after struggling to recover.

articles.title: Nasser: Pietersen could be key for 'second coming' of Banton
articles.summary: Nasser Hussain has lauded the "second coming" of England batter Tom Banton and says the appointment of new white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen could be key to his development in the middle order.
body: Banton top-scored for England with an unbeaten 52 off 24 balls in an impressive innings, combining well with skipper Harry Brook (23 off 8) after Jos Buttler (30 off 16) had become the first player to make 15,000 T20 runs - as the home side sauntered past Sri Lanka's modest 145-9 with 7.5 overs to spare.
The half-century was Banton's third since re-entering the white-ball set-up as a middle-order batter, having played as an opener in his early career - a transition Hussain lauded on Sky Sports.
"Banton has been really good in his second coming [after moving from opener to the middle order]," said Hussain.
"Everyone talks about what [white-ball mentor] Kevin Pietersen can do for Harry Brook, but I think Pietersen could be good for Banton.

articles.title: Allen stars as Bills open new stadium with win over Lions
articles.summary: Josh Allen quickly put his stamp on the Buffalo Bills' new Highmark Stadium as he threw three touchdown passes and ran for two scores as the Bills beat the Detroit Lions 41-31 on Thursday night.
body: It was Allen's fourth career five-TD outing, and followed a four-touchdown outing (two passing, two rushing) in Buffalo's 36-31 season-opening win at Houston.
The $2.1bn stadium that officially opened last month was built across the street from the Bills' former home.
Allen followed the pre-game fireworks celebration with more fireworks of his own by overseeing touchdown drives on each of Buffalo's first four possessions.

He scored the first regular-season TD in the stadium on a 1-yard run 5:51 into the opening quarter. He followed that with a 43-yard scoring pass to a wide-open Josh Palmer. Tight ends Dalton Kincaid, with a 16-yard catch, and Dawson Knox, with a 1-yarder, also scored for Buffalo in the first half.

articles.title: Azerbaijan GP schedule: Why is the race on a Saturday?
articles.summary: Formula 1 will race in Azerbaijan on a Saturday as the sport returns to the Baku City Circuit for what often proves one of the season's most incident-filled events.
body: The first round of a flyaway triple header before trips to Malaysia and Singapore, the Baku race weekend starts a day earlier than normal meaning Practice is on Thursday, Qualifying is on Friday and the Grand Prix is on the Saturday.

Kimi Antonelli leads the world championship by 81 points after consecutive wins in Monza and Madrid and time is running out for his would-be title challengers to put a run together to rival him with a scheduled eight rounds left after Baku.

But, as then-title leader Oscar Piastri found to his cost at last year's race, the wall-lined Baku circuit can certainly bite if you make a mistake with challenges present all round the fast and tricky layout for both qualifying and race day.
The Baku race takes place a day earlier than normal on a Saturday (September 26) as it is the country's Remembrance Day on Sunday September 27.
